subject: Clearwell production - quota translation gap and next steps
messages:
From: Jenna Park <jenna.park@clearwell.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@clearwell.ai
Date: 2026-06-20T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Degraded: unexpected 429s across prod - ticket #5641

Hi Irene,

We started seeing a flurry of 429s across our production API starting at ~08:55 PDT this morning. The errors are for both embedding and generation endpoints and appear to affect ~20% of requests coming from our primary region. We rolled some quick client-side retries but wanted to escalate to you immediately as this looks like a server-side quota enforcement issue.

Quick details:
- Request IDs: a sample attached in diagnostic-trace-2026-06-20.txt (see attachment).
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings
- Impact window: 08:55 - ongoing as of 09:15

Can you confirm whether this is related to any quota change or routing/overlap with a dedicated pool? We have a production traffic spike today due to a scheduled campaign and would like a mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Jenna Park
Head of Platform Ops, Clearwell Health

Attachments: diagnostic-trace-2026-06-20.txt
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Degraded: unexpected 429s across prod - ticket #5641

Hi Jenna — thanks for the heads up and the trace. We're triaging now. Initial notes:

- I've opened an internal incident and tagged the quota/routing team.
- From the trace snippets you sent, the token counts look normal; the 429 payloads indicate "quota_exceeded: tenant_quota" rather than per-model throttling. That suggests a quota translation/mapping problem on our side.
- Can you confirm whether any of your requests are being routed to our dedicated pool alias (you can check the x-redwood-pool header)? If so, paste an example request id.

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Attach the full request headers for two failing requests (IDs in the trace).
2) Confirm whether you've recently changed any API keys or added new sub-tenants.

I'll propose a short mitigation in my next email after we confirm routing.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@clearwell.ai>, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-20T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Degraded: unexpected 429s across prod - ticket #5641

Folks — quick update from triage and an immediate mitigation path we can apply while we root-cause: 

Findings so far:
- Root cause (preliminary): a configuration translation bug in the dedicated/reserved capacity mapping service. When a customer had both hosted and dedicated aliases, our mapping layer applied the tenant quota from the hosted tier to requests ending up on the dedicated pool in certain routing edge cases. Those requests then hit a lower effective quota and returned 429s.
- Repro: reproduced in staging with Clearwell's quota-mapping.csv (attached).

Immediate mitigation (15–30 min action, low risk):
1) Temporarily relax the effective quota enforcement for Clearwell tenant_id: clearwell-89 for the dedicated pool only (config change via feature flag). This will allow in-flight traffic to clear while preserving published limits on hosted tiers.
2) Add a fallback routing rule: if a request receives a quota_exceeded from dedicated pool BUT the tenant has an active hosted quota, route to hosted as a temporary fallback for the next 2 hours.

Longer-term fixes:
- Deploy fix to mapping service to correctly honor pool-specific quotas; targeted patch in next patch window (ETA 48 hours).
- Add unit test and e2e scenario to prevent regression.

Attachments: quota-mapping.csv (sample), redwood-incident-summary.pdf (brief).

If Clearwell approves, we can run the temporary relax + fallback now. I've scheduled the config change with the ops runbook and will execute on approval.

—Rafael Mendes
Lead Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jenna Park <jenna.park@clearwell.ai>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@clearwell.ai
Date: 2026-06-21T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Degraded: unexpected 429s across prod - ticket #5641

Thanks Rafael & Irene — that sounds right based on what we saw. We gave the green light to the temporary relax/fallback and can confirm that error rates dropped to baseline within ~20 minutes of the change. Much appreciated.

Two follow-ups from us:
- Will the temporary relax reset any counters that would cause a spike once turned back on? We want to avoid a secondary surge when you re-enable strict enforcement.
- Please send a postmortem and the timeline for the permanent fix. Our compliance folks will want the SLA window documented.

We can join a post-incident review if you'd like to schedule one.

Best,
Jenna
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@clearwell.ai>
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-22T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident actions: Clearwell quota translation gap (summary + next steps)

Hi Jenna — thanks again for the fast confirmation yesterday and for the test traces you provided. Below is a concise summary and our action plan; I'll also drop the formal postmortem doc into the Drive link.

What happened (summary):
- A configuration translation bug caused some requests routed to the dedicated pool to be evaluated with the hosted-tier quota, which in specific routing edge cases made them hit a lower effective cap and return 429s.
- Impact window: 2026-06-20 08:55 PDT — 2026-06-20 09:15 PDT (primary spike) with follow-up residual retries happening through the morning.
- Customer impact: intermittent 429s for ~20% of Clearwell's requests during the window; mitigated by temporary relax + fallback.

Immediate actions completed:
- Applied temporary relax to dedicated pool enforcement for tenant clearwell-89 (2026-06-20 10:05 PDT) — removed within 2 hours after traffic normalized.
- Enabled fallback routing for quota_exceeded responses while we pushed the mapping fix.
- Correlated traces and verified request ids in diagnostic-trace-2026-06-20.txt.

Planned remediation and timeline:
1) Code fix to mapping service: patch merged and scheduled for deployment to prod on 2026-06-24 (ETA 48 hours from last working session).
2) Add E2E test case and monitoring alert: by 2026-07-02.
3) Quota enforcement policy update and runbook change to make the fallback automatic for any tenant with mixed pool aliases: by 2026-07-10.

We're also offering a complimentary one-week backlog of doubled burst credits (applied to your account) to offset any cost from retries during the incident window. If that's acceptable, we'll apply it and send a billing note.

Next steps for us (action items):
- Rafael: deploy mapping fix and confirm post-deploy validation checks (owner: rafael_mendes).
- Monica: update runbook and alerting (owner: monica_patel).
- Irene: schedule a 30-min post-incident review with Clearwell and share the full postmortem (owner: irene_choi).

Would you prefer the post-incident review this Friday (2026-06-25 09:00 PDT) or early next week?

Links and attachments: quota-mapping.csv, diagnostic-trace-2026-06-20.txt, redwood-incident-summary.pdf, postmortem draft: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cClearwellPostmortem

Thanks again for working through this with us — we'll be in touch as each action completes.

—Irene Choi
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
